title: Hybrid priority fanout and timeboxed prefilter for rank service
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: tail latency on the reranking endpoint spikes when candidate sets contain a few long-token items and many short ones. Current monolithic scoring path blocks on worst-case decoding and thrashes KV cache, which increases P95/P99 and causes timeouts. Goal: reduce tail latency and variability while preserving ranking quality (NDCG) and throughput for high-concurrency workloads. Approach: implement a two-stage hybrid fanout where a lightweight prefilter micromodel quickly prunes candidates, and a priority fanout routes items into fast and slow scoring lanes with timeboxed execution and soft backpressure. Return partial ranked lists when deadline elapses with graceful quality degradation and rollbacks if regression observed.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped design alternatives with product and research. Evaluated three options: 1) strict token caps + drop, 2) approximate prefilter + full scoring for top-K, 3) speculative decoding hedging. We chose option 2 as best quality/latency trade-off.

2026-02-18 - Design review: landed on a prefilter micromodel (cheap transformer distil, ~5M params) to score candidates for likely relevance. It runs with batching separate from full scorer. Fast-lane handles candidates with prefilter score >= threshold and short token length; slow-lane receives rest.

2026-02-25 - Implementation: added lane scheduler module (rerank/orchestrator/lane_scheduler.go). Implemented token_governor to enforce per-request token ceilings and per-GPU soft quotas. Initial unit tests for lane assignment and token accounting added.

2026-03-01 - Integration test: verified timeboxed prefilter reduces median scorer calls by ~48% on synthetic workload. P95 improved by ~23% but P99 still elevated for very skewed candidate distributions. Investigating KV cache eviction patterns.

2026-03-03 - PR feedback from runtime team: tighten invariants around KV cache pinning for fast-lane decodes; ensure fallback path does not double-decode same KV segment. Added instrumentation to mark cache hits per-lane.

2026-03-05 - Experiment plan finalized: canary rollout with feature flag, first to 1% traffic for 48h, evaluate latency and NDCG drop (target <0.5% NDCG regression), then 10% for 72h, then ramp. Metrics dashboard and alerts created.
Open items: tuning prefilter threshold per-customer workload, exploring prefix caching to further reduce duplicate KV work for slow-lane.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 and P99 latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=15% on production-like traces under mixed candidate-length workloads. 2) End-to-end NDCG drop <=0.5% vs baseline on holdout eval set. 3) No increase in error rate or timeouts. 4) Observability: per-lane latency, prefilter recall, token-governor enforced, and streamable partial responses verified.
implementation_notes: Modules: rerank/orchestrator (fanout + lane scheduler), rerank/prefilter (distilled micromodel container), rerank/scorer lanes (fast / slow), token_governor (per-request and per-GPU soft quotas), streaming partial-responses API. Use feature flag 'rerank.hybrid_prefilter' and runtime overrides per-customer. Add metrics: prefilter_recall, prefilter_precision, lane_assignment_ratio, lane_kv_cache_hit, tokens_charged, partial_return_rate.
rollout_plan: Feature flag + canary. 1) Deploy prefilter and lane scheduler behind feature flag in staging. 2) Canary 1% traffic for 48h, auto-rollback on latency or NDCG breach. 3) Ramp to 10% for 72h, analyze per-customer impact. 4) Full rollout with retroactive monitoring for 2 weeks. Postmortem if >0.5% long-term quality drift.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lane assignment and token_governor. Integration tests with synthetic candidate mixes (short-only, uniform, long-tail). End-to-end A/B jobs against production holdout for NDCG and latency. Load-run experiments to validate KV cache behavior at 75% and 120% baseline concurrency.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: prefilter false negatives reduce quality. Mitigation: conservative threshold left default; monitor recall metric and increase scorer budget if recall drops. Risk: KV cache thrash from slow-lane bursts. Mitigation: pin hot KV segments for fast-lane and stagger slow-lane decode windows. Risk: complexity increases operational surface. Mitigation: rollback via feature flag and granular per-customer toggles.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on correctness of token accounting, interactions with KV cache pinning, and ensuring the fast-lane scorer never bypasses quota checks. Reviewers: please validate perf assumptions in rerank/orchestrator and signal any hidden coupling with existing batching layer.
qa_checks: Smoke test on staging with 10k requests, verify partial-results format and downstream client compatibility. Confirm telemetry tags include feature_flag and lane_id.
expected_metrics: Improve P95 by >=15%, P99 by >=10% for mixed workloads; prefilter should reduce full-scorer calls by ~40-60% depending on workload; prefilter_recall >= 0.98 on curated eval set.
